images.caption: Fig. 2:Training pipeline and policy architecture.Stage 1 learns whole-body control by training the state-policy teacher with PPO. Stage 2 learns the object dynamics: it initializes the privileged encoder and decoder latent-input weights by matching teacher actions, then jointly refines the encoder and decoder with PPO. Human motion examples supply reference tracking and an AMP style reward. Stage 3 learns visual grounding by predicting the latent from RGB-D histories and camera ego-motion, using box-state supervision and DAgger rollouts. The pretrained CNN and heatmap head stay fixed during GRU training; the privileged encoder and decoder remain fixed throughout Stage 3. The decoder also receives robot/reference observations. Because Stage 3 learns only the latent predictor, the visual controller reuses the PPO-trained decoder without modification.

Fig. 3:Throw and appearance variations.Simulation examples show changes in release distance, box size, color, and landing location. The box-size panel illustrates measured real boxes; simulated weight and distance tests use the 34×\times26×\times22 cm training box. Color augmentation is applied when training the visual component. These variations define the operating conditions evaluated in Tab.I.

Fig. 5:Real-robot catching across throw distances, box sizes, payloads, and lateral offsets.Successful trials at 2.5, 5, and 7 m and with small, regular, and large boxes (left, each at release, during approach, and after the catch), with 0.5, 1, and 2 kg payloads (right; weighing views show the payload mass), and with lateral offsets of 0.9 m right and 0.7 m left (bottom). Insets show onboard camera views; timestamps indicate elapsed time within each sequence. White outlines mark box positions and dashed curves indicate flight direction. The same visual latent controller succeeds at every tested distance, box size, payload, and lateral offset; Tab.IIreports catch rates for distance, size, and payload, and Sec.V-Fthe lateral-offset rate.
